title: Mining Engineer Salary: Converting Hourly Pay to Annual, Fortnightly, and After Tax
description: Learn how to convert a mining engineer salary from hourly to annual using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and comparisons with the National Minimum Wage.
salarySummary: Based on the ABS mining industry average of $3224.20 per week, a 38-hour week gives an hourly rate of about $84.85 and an annual gross of $167,658.40.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $84.85 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $167,658.40 per year. This formula assumes consistent hours and no unpaid overtime.

faqs.q: What is the average mining engineer salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time ordinary time earnings in the mining industry averaged $3224.20 per week as of May 2026. This is an industry average, not a job median for mining engineers. Using a 38-hour week, that equates to roughly $84.85 per hour. Individual salaries vary by experience, location, and employer.

faqs.q: How much tax and super will I pay on a mining engineer salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 year, resident tax rates apply: nil up to $18,200, 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top by your employer, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For a $167,658 annual salary, estimated tax and Medicare are about $46,467, leaving around $121,192 net. Super adds about $20,119 to your total package.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the 38-hour week and annual pay

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to see how they compare on an annual basis. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. In Australia, full-time work is commonly based on a 38-hour week, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. We use 38 hours unless you know your actual weekly hours are different. This gives you a gross annual figure before tax and other deductions.

For example, if you earn $84.85 per hour (which we’ll explore below), working 38 hours each week for 52 weeks gives:

$84.85 × 38 × 52 = $167,658.40 per year.

You can also work out your fortnightly pay by multiplying your weekly pay by two. Weekly pay is hourly rate × 38, so fortnightly is that amount doubled. For the same rate, weekly is $3,224.30 and fortnightly is $6,448.60.

## The mining engineer salary: an industry average

You may be searching for a **mining engineer salary** to benchmark an offer or your current pay. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings survey for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in the mining industry were $3,224.20 per week. This is an **industry average**, not a job median for mining engineers. It includes all full-time roles in mining, not just engineers. Still, it gives a useful reference point.

Dividing that weekly figure by 38 hours gives an hourly rate of approximately $84.85. So if you hear of a mining engineer salary around that level, it aligns with the industry average. But remember: your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your experience, location, and employer.

For comparison, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates for professional engineers may be higher than the minimum but still below the mining average. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement.

## Tax, Medicare, and super on your annual pay

Once you have your gross annual figure, you can estimate your take-home pay. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% on the excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. (Note: the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.)

For a mining engineer salary of $167,658.40 (using the industry average):

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000: 15% of $26,800 = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$135,000: 30% of $90,000 = $27,000
- Tax on $135,001–$167,658.40: 37% of $32,658.40 = $12,083.61
- Total tax: $43,103.61
- Medicare (2%): $3,353.17
- Total deductions: $46,456.78
- Net annual income: approximately $121,201.62

Your fortnightly take-home would be about $4,661.60 (net annual divided by 26).

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top by your employer. For $167,658.40, that’s $20,119.01, provided your earnings are below the $270,830 maximum contribution base. So your total employment package (salary plus super) would be around $187,777.41.

## Using the timesheet to calculate your own figures

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: if you are a casual employee, your base rate already includes the casual loading? No – the timesheet has a checkbox to add 25% on top of the base rate you type. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading; type your base award or minimum rate and check the box if applicable.

For more details on award rates and pay guides, visit [pay guides](/blog). You can also explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for other industries, or [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for different work patterns.

## Important notes and disclaimers

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Comparing with the National Minimum Wage and awards

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for full-time adults. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates for professional engineers may be higher, but the mining industry average is well above these minimums. If you are covered by an award, check the specific classification on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

## Final thoughts on the mining engineer salary

While the ABS average gives a useful benchmark, your actual **mining engineer salary** will depend on your qualifications, experience, and the specific employer. Use the formula and our timesheet to convert any hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures. Always consider super as part of your total compensation package.
